declared_purpose: Monitor user-selected topics through scheduled web searches, RSS/Atom feeds and GitHub releases; filter and deduplicate results, score importance and sentiment, produce contextual alerts and weekly digests, and track state. These features are explicit; particular stored fields, automatic search queries and retention periods are implementation choices (SKILL.md:4-4,24-24,52-66).

data_operations.operation: Collect, read, persist and display configuration
data_operations.source: Setup answers, CLI arguments and config.json
data_operations.data_scope: Topic names, queries, keywords, feed URLs, repositories, context, schedules, alert conditions and channels. Configuration is plain JSON.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Skill-local config.json; configuration summaries return to the caller through stdout.
data_operations.condition: Setup, quick-add and topic-management paths. The setup wizard can overwrite existing configuration after its own confirmation.

data_operations.source: The OPML file supplied to import-opml
data_operations.data_scope: Outline titles, xmlUrl and htmlUrl values; imported monitoring settings and context. htmlUrl also becomes a search query when the topic lacks one.
data_operations.condition: import-opml; matching topics merge feed subscriptions, while other outlines create topics. An htmlUrl additionally triggers the discovery operation below.

data_operations.source: Explicit discovery URLs, add/edit --discover-feeds arguments, or imported OPML htmlUrl values
data_operations.data_scope: Requested URL, User-Agent and Accept headers; up to 250,000 response bytes. Extracted alternate links and five guessed paths form the returned candidate list.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Requested website and any redirect destination reached by urlopen; response processing is local. Callers may print candidates or save them in config.json.
data_operations.condition: Discovery invocation. Recognized feed suffixes return immediately without fetching. Candidate links are returned without validation.

data_operations.operation: Pass search data and credentials to a local subprocess
data_operations.data_scope: Control-character-stripped query capped at 500 characters, a five-result request, PATH, HOME, LANG, TERM, SERPER_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY, EXA_API_KEY, YOU_API_KEY, SEARXNG_INSTANCE_URL and WSP_CACHE_DIR when present.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: web-search-plus search.py at WEB_SEARCH_PLUS_PATH or the computed sibling path. Its stdout returns to monitor.py; downstream provider disclosure and caching are unresolved.
data_operations.condition: A nonempty query and an existing search script, including during --dry-run. Verbose mode prints the sanitized query and selected diagnostics; timeout handling prints the original query. Mock results are only a dry-run fallback.

data_operations.operation: Poll remote feeds and conditionally authenticate
data_operations.source: Configured feeds, github_repos and saved feed validators
data_operations.data_scope: Feed URL, User-Agent, Accept and encoding headers, and cached ETag/Last-Modified validators. URL-embedded HTTP credentials become Basic authentication; the vendored handler can retry using Digest authentication.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured feed servers, github.com release feeds, and redirect destinations handled by the URL handler. Entire response bodies are read into local memory.
data_operations.condition: Feed collection, including --dry-run; duplicate configured feed URLs are consolidated. HTTP 304 responses skip entry processing. These are direct network operations despite documentation claiming no direct HTTP.

data_operations.operation: Read or parse feed input locally
data_operations.source: Configured feed strings and retrieved feed bodies
data_operations.data_scope: feedparser accepts streams, supported URL schemes and local filenames. Monitor converts at most ten parsed entries per feed into title, URL, full normalized summary, publication date, tags and source metadata.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local parser and monitor memory; projected results subsequently enter scoring, findings or alert paths.
data_operations.condition: The value passed as a feed determines whether resource access is remote or local. A local filename or file URL can cause a local read; this does not itself upload that file.

data_operations.operation: Filter results and infer importance and sentiment
data_operations.source: Result titles, snippets, URLs and publication dates; topic keywords, source preferences and alert conditions
data_operations.data_scope: Relevance score, priority, scoring reason, positive/negative/neutral/mixed sentiment and sentiment-shift status. These describe findings, not an inferred user mood.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local Python processing; inferred values subsequently accompany state, findings and alerts.
data_operations.condition: Results with URLs that survive deduplication and boolean filters. Scoring uses local rules; no model-service request appears in this component.

data_operations.source: Prior state, processed result URLs, feed responses and monitoring counters
data_operations.data_scope: MD5 URL hashes with timestamps; feed URLs, validators, check/status metadata, site URLs and feed titles; topic check times, result counts and alert counts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: topic-monitor-state.json under TOPIC_MONITOR_DATA_DIR, defaulting to skill-local .data/.
data_operations.condition: State is loaded for monitoring and testing. Loading can create directories. Normal monitor execution saves state; --dry-run suppresses the final state write. Expired deduplication entries are checked but not removed.

data_operations.source: Every scored, nonduplicate result that passes topic filters
data_operations.data_scope: Timestamp, sentiment, result URL and title; last_sentiment. Each topic retains at most 50 history entries.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Topic records in the local monitor state file.
data_operations.condition: Non-dry-run monitoring, including low-priority results and topics with sentiment-shift alerts disabled. The shift comparison itself reads only the previous sentiment.

data_operations.source: Collected result dictionaries and derived scoring values
data_operations.data_scope: Entire result dictionary, score, reason, timestamp, sentiment and shift flag. Search-provider fields are not projected to a fixed schema before storage.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: findings/YYYY-MM-DD_topic-id.json under the configured data directory.
data_operations.condition: Medium-priority results during non-dry-run monitoring. Existing daily findings are loaded and appended; no findings cleanup path is supplied.

data_operations.source: Topic configuration, high-priority result and scoring output
data_operations.data_scope: Topic identifiers, title, full snippet, URL, context, rendered message, score/reason, sentiment, source, feed URL, repository and delivery status.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: alerts-queue.json under the configured data directory; stdout receives a short ALERT_QUEUED announcement.
data_operations.condition: Non-dry-run high-priority results passing rate limits, iterated over topic channels. This path does not consult global channel enabled settings. Queueing is local persistence, not platform delivery.

data_operations.operation: Return alert previews and delivery envelopes
data_operations.source: Topic/result data or pending local queue records; TOPIC_MONITOR_TELEGRAM_ID
data_operations.data_scope: Rendered alert includes topic, title, a bounded snippet, complete configured context, source/link, scoring reason and sentiment. JSON processing also includes routing metadata and the Telegram target variable for every channel.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: stdout to the invoking caller, potentially an OpenClaw agent. Telegram, Discord and email are intended downstream channels; actual transmission is not implemented here.
data_operations.condition: Dry-run alert previews or process_alerts.py human/JSON output. Returning JSON does not itself prove remote disclosure or further persistence.

data_operations.operation: Mark delivered alerts and delete aged queue entries
data_operations.source: Local alert queue and supplied alert IDs or age threshold
data_operations.data_scope: Marking adds sent and sent_at without removing payloads. Age cleanup removes both sent and unsent records older than the cutoff; invalid timestamps are retained.
data_operations.condition: Explicit --mark-sent or --clear-old HOURS invocation. Cleanup is not automatically scheduled by the packaged monitoring flow.

data_operations.operation: Read findings and return a weekly digest
data_operations.source: Date-matching local findings files and current topic configuration
data_operations.data_scope: Topic names, titles, links, scores, reasons and sentiments; full snippets for three highlights and shortened snippets for up to five entries per topic.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local aggregation and stdout to the caller. No digest file write or channel transmission is implemented.
data_operations.condition: digest.py preview/default or --send, with optional --week-offset. The --send path prints the digest and a success message.

data_operations.source: config.json and the requested topic ID
data_operations.data_scope: Deletes the matching topic configuration. Associated findings, queued alerts, sentiment history and feed state are not deleted by this command.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Rewritten config.json; historical data remains at its separate data-directory boundaries.
data_operations.condition: manage_topics.py remove for an existing topic.

data_operations.source: Configured digest schedule and computed skill/script paths
data_operations.data_scope: Schedules and commands containing absolute local paths.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: JSON on stdout to the caller; intended for OpenClaw's cron tool.
data_operations.condition: setup_cron.py. The packaged script does not install jobs or modify crontab.

data_operations.operation: Read and print standalone parser test input
data_operations.source: A supplied local filename, default test.html, or stdin
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local parser memory and diagnostic stdout.
data_operations.condition: Direct execution of vendored sgmllib.py; its default test class prints parsed data. This entry point is not invoked by importing it for monitoring.

potential_excess.data_scope: Automatically invented topic searches and OPML htmlUrl search queries
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: web-search-plus search.py subprocess; ultimate search-provider recipient is unresolved.
potential_excess.condition: Quick-add with feeds/repositories still defaults to a search query; OPML import populates otherwise empty queries from htmlUrl.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The skill supports combining sources, but feed subscription and release monitoring do not explicitly require an additional web search.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Poll selected feeds and releases; retain searches explicitly requested by the user.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Make generated web searches opt-in for feed/repository setup and OPML import. This removes a potentially redundant action, rather than trimming a required search payload.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve explicit queries and intentional mixed-source monitoring.

potential_excess.data_scope: OPML htmlUrl requests and additional discovered or guessed feed subscriptions
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Each imported htmlUrl website during discovery; additional subscriptions in config.json and subsequent feed servers.
potential_excess.condition: An imported outline contains both an explicit xmlUrl and htmlUrl.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Importing the supplied feed subscription is explicit; visiting its website and expanding subscriptions is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Read and save the supplied xmlUrl and subscription title.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Import explicit subscriptions directly and offer website discovery separately. This removes an additional request and subscription-expansion action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep discovery available when requested or when resolving a missing feed URL.

potential_excess.data_scope: Original query characters omitted from the actual search request, including content beyond the 500-character limit
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: stderr returned to the caller; any subsequent log retention is unknown.
potential_excess.condition: The search subprocess times out; this diagnostic is not restricted to verbose mode.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Failure diagnostics are useful, but the original unbounded query exceeds the query used by the search action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify the failed topic and timeout.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Log the topic ID and timeout, or at most the same sanitized query prefix sent to the child.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain enough identification to troubleshoot the failed search.

potential_excess.data_scope: Expired MD5 URL hashes and last-seen timestamps
potential_excess.condition: Normal monitoring accumulates entries beyond deduplication_window_hours; expiry changes matching behavior but does not delete records.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Deduplication is explicit, with a configured time window. Indefinite retention beyond that window is unnecessary for the implemented check.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Recognize URLs seen inside the active deduplication window.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Prune entries older than the active window before saving state.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Use the current configured window; preserve longer history only if retrospective window expansion is an intended requirement.

potential_excess.condition: Feed responses contain a site link or title.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Conditional polling requires validators and check metadata; these two persisted descriptive fields are not consumed by the supplied polling or result-conversion path.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain ETag/Last-Modified values and required check metadata; use the current parsed title when producing results.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit unused site_url and feed_title copies from persisted cache records.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain them only if an additional feed-management display or other consumer requires them.

potential_excess.data_scope: Result titles and URLs attached to each sentiment-history entry
potential_excess.condition: Every scored result during non-dry-run monitoring, including low-priority findings and topics without shift alerts.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Sentiment history is explicitly declared; retaining finding identifiers alongside every label is an implementation choice. Shift detection reads only the preceding label.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Track sentiment labels and compare the previous label when shift alerts are enabled.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Retain a bounded label history and any needed timestamps; omit titles and URLs unless a history-view feature requires them.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve declared sentiment tracking and the previous label required for shift detection.

potential_excess.data_scope: Whole result dictionaries, including unused feed metadata and any additional fields returned by web-search-plus
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Daily findings JSON files under FINDINGS_DIR
potential_excess.condition: A result receives medium priority during non-dry-run monitoring.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Saving findings for digests is required; serializing every returned field is extra data within that required persistence action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain titles, URLs, digest snippets and the scoring/sentiment metadata consumed by digest generation.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Project results to an explicit digest schema before saving, excluding unused provider and feed fields.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve snippets needed for highlights and historical --week-offset digests; do not impose a shorter archive window without a corresponding retention requirement.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full snippets and duplicate context/reason/sentiment components, plus source/feed/repository fields accompanying an already rendered message
potential_excess.condition: monitor.py queues a new alert with message already populated. The message bounds its snippet, while the separate snippet field retains the full value.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Reliable queued delivery is necessary; duplicate rendering inputs and unused source fields are extra data in that persistence action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain the rendered message, delivery state, routing information and metadata consumed by the human/JSON output formats.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: For new pre-rendered records, omit unused raw rendering inputs and source fields. Retain component-based rendering only for records lacking message.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve existing queue compatibility, JSON metadata, human previews and delivery acknowledgments.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete delivered alert payloads, including topic context and result content
potential_excess.condition: Alerts are marked sent and explicit age cleanup is never invoked.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The queue supports pending delivery. Keeping completed payloads indefinitely is not required by its supplied consumers.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep pending alerts until acknowledged and retain any required delivery bookkeeping.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Automatically remove or reduce acknowledged records after a defined retry/audit interval.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not delete unacknowledged alerts merely because they are old; preserve any explicitly required delivery-history period.

potential_excess.data_scope: TOPIC_MONITOR_TELEGRAM_ID on Discord, email or other non-Telegram alert envelopes
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: stdout JSON returned by process_alerts.py --json to its caller/OpenClaw agent
potential_excess.condition: A pending non-Telegram alert is formatted while the Telegram target environment variable is populated.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Routing requires the selected channel's destination; attaching a Telegram destination to every channel is extra data in the required return.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Return the appropriate destination for each alert's channel.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Include TOPIC_MONITOR_TELEGRAM_ID only for Telegram alerts; resolve other destinations through their applicable channel mechanism.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve Telegram routing and the caller's ability to deliver other channels. No onward disclosure to those platforms is established by this code.

unknowns: Downstream search assessment is blocked by absent web-search-plus source: provider selection, exact outbound payloads, credential use, WSP_CACHE_DIR contents and retention cannot be determined. Passing allowed environment variables to its local subprocess does not establish disclosure of all credentials to search providers.

Actual OpenClaw message and cron behavior is outside the package. Platform transmission, final recipients, delivery acknowledgments and retention of returned output remain unresolved. The packaged digest sender only prints.

Runtime configuration, OPML content, environment and provider responses are not supplied. Concrete feed hosts, channel destinations, embedded credentials and additional result fields are therefore unknown.

Memory-aware summaries are declared, but the supplied implementation uses configured context. No packaged path reads past conversations or personal-analytics data; learning_enabled does not establish such collection.

The supplied inventory has no .gitignore supporting the README's state-file exclusion claim. Filesystem access controls, backups and external storage behavior for TOPIC_MONITOR_DATA_DIR are also unknown.
